legal.immutabilityNotice: An approved version is never edited: people signed exactly that text. A correction is a new version. A draft can be deleted.
legal.readOnlyNotice: Approved version: its text is fixed. To change the wording, start the next version from this one; the old one stays as it was.
legal.nextVersion: Start the next version from this one

pdf.draftNotice: DRAFT — unapproved version. The text below has no effect until it is approved and may still change.

legal.newFromIntro: Prefilled from version {version}. Change what needs changing, save the draft, read it, then approve it. Version {version} stays as it is.
legal.noTranslations: This version has no text yet.
legal.newFromTemplateIntro: Prefilled with the template's text. Left to fill, in both languages, in angle brackets: {blanks}. Save the draft, then approve it from its page.
legal.tokensHelp: In the declaration only, these fields are filled in automatically for each person and event: '{{participant}}' (the registered name), '{{participantIdDocument}}' (their identity document, typed at signing), '{{guardian}}' and '{{guardianIdDocument}}' (a minor's parent or guardian and their document; a dash for an adult), '{{idDocument}}' (the declarant's document — the parent's, for a minor), '{{event}}' (the event's title), '{{eventDate}}' (its date), '{{eventLocation}}' (its place), '{{minimumAge}}' (the event's minimum age, with its unit), '{{signedAt}}' (the moment of signing). Written exactly so, with double braces.
legal.newIntro: You are writing a new version, not changing an existing one. It saves as a draft and is not public until you approve it.
legal.bodyHelp: A blank line separates paragraphs; ## at the start makes a heading. Link: [words](https://…). Picture, on its own line: ![what it shows](https://…), from Gallery → Pictures.
legal.keyLocked: The document cannot change after creation.
legal.editorWarning: This is the club’s legal text. Write or paste only wording the club has approved — never invent legal content.
legal.approveHelp: Once approved the text is public and can no longer be edited. A later correction means a new version.
legal.approveConfirm: I confirm the club has approved this text and it may become public
legal.legalVersionApproved: The version is approved and now public.
legal.termsRegistrations: Registrations while it was in force: {count}
legal.deleteBody: The draft and its text in both languages go permanently. Nobody has seen it: a draft is never public and nobody has signed it.
legal.deleteBlockedApproved: Approved — cannot be deleted. What the club published stays on the record.
legal.deleteBlockedReferenced: Cannot be deleted: {signatures}, {events} and {acknowledgements} depend on this version.
legal.deleteBlockedTermsAccepted: Cannot be deleted: registrations were submitted or declarations signed while it was in force, {window} ({count}), and neither records which version of the terms was accepted.
legal.newFromTemplateComplete: Prefilled with the template's text and the club's facts, complete. Read it all, save the draft, then approve it from its page.
legal.platformApproved: Done: the missing texts are approved ({count}), with the club's facts. Registration is open.

platform.title: One step: approve the templates with the club's facts
platform.intro: Not yet approved: {keys}. The button below creates and approves, in your name, version 1 of each from its template, with the facts below written in. A text already approved is not touched.

facts.contactEmail: Contact email — the address shown, from Pages → Contact

platform.contactFactMissing: EMAIL_REPLY_TO, or the club's Gmail under «Contact address shown», on Pages → Contact
platform.blocked: Not yet possible: the variables {variables} are missing from the project's settings (Vercel → Settings → Environment Variables). Set them, redeploy, and the button appears here.
platform.consequence: Pressing it, you approve these texts for the club: they take effect on the site, and a correction is a new version. You can read them first, below.
platform.button: Approve the missing texts now ({count} of {total})

legal.withdrawBody: Nothing is deleted: the version stays on the record, with its number. It is only no longer offered: not public, not choosable on an event.
legal.withdrawBlockedCurrent: In force right now — it cannot be withdrawn. Approve its successor first; then this one can go.
legal.withdrawnNotice: This version was withdrawn on {date}. Its text stays here, on the record, with its number, but it no longer appears publicly and can no longer be chosen on an event.
legal.legalVersionWithdrawn: The version has been withdrawn. It stays on the record, with its number, but is no longer offered anywhere.

startFrom.title: Start from the template
startFrom.orBlank: Or write from nothing, in the form below.
startFrom.help: 1. Pick the template (or Regenerate all) · 2. Read, fill in and “Save draft” · 3. Approve — only then is it in force.

tokens.title: The fields that fill themselves in
tokens.intro: Leave them exactly as they are. The participant's and the event's are filled in at signing; the deadlines, with the values under Settings → “Deadlines”.
tokens.participant: The name the participant registered under
tokens.declarant: Whoever signs: the participant, or the parent or guardian for a minor
tokens.guardian: The parent or guardian when the participant is a minor; a dash otherwise
tokens.idDocument: The declarant's identity document (the parent's, for a minor), typed at signing — never scanned
tokens.participantIdDocument: The participant's own identity document — the minor's, for a minor — typed at signing. With it in the text a minor signs too, beside the parent; without it, only the parent signs
tokens.guardianIdDocument: The parent's or guardian's document when the participant is a minor; a dash otherwise
tokens.eventDate: The event's date, in its own zone
tokens.confirmationHours: How long the address confirmation link is valid, from “Deadlines”
tokens.holdMinutes: How long a place is held for signing, from “Deadlines”
tokens.offerHours: How long a waiting-list offer stays open, from “Deadlines”
tokens.reminderClause: The reminder as a clause with its comma, from “Deadlines”; with no number when the club sends none by default
tokens.minimumAge: The event's minimum age, with its unit (“16 years”): at least 14 for a race, at least 18 for a group run. Every declaration states it in a sentence of its own
tokens.participantListStates: Privacy notice only: the three stages beside a name on the public list. Without it in the notice in force, only confirmed names
tokens.participantListSocials: Privacy notice only: the tick with which someone shows their Strava and Instagram on the public list. Without it in the notice in force, never
tokens.participantListNumbers: Privacy notice only (and the terms): the race number beside the names of the confirmed on the public list. Without it in the notice in force, the list shows no number
tokens.publicListPeriod: Privacy notice only: how long the public participant list stays up after the event, from “Deadlines”, unit included; after that the list closes by itself
tokens.newsletterTopics: Privacy notice only: the topics of the contact page's subscription. Without it in the notice in force, the subscription does not show
tokens.teamPage: Privacy notice only: the team page's name, in quotation marks. With it in the notice in force, /admin/tasks counts the page as described
tokens.series: Only in the group-run declarations: the series' name, when the run repeats. The sentence that names it shows only for a series; a one-day run keeps the sentence with '{{event}}' and '{{eventDate}}'
tokens.seriesRhythm: Only in the group-run declarations: how often the series repeats, read off its dates (“every Tuesday at 18:30”)
tokens.seriesPlace: Only in the group-run declarations: the series' usual starting place
tokens.promotionalMaterials: Only in the privacy notice: the optional box for offers and benefits from the club and its partners. Without it in the notice in force, the form does not offer it
tokens.promotionalMaterialsShared: Only in the privacy notice: what data the club's partners may receive from those who ticked offers and benefits. Without it in the notice in force, the list for sponsors is off
tokens.registrationsPerAddress: Terms only: how many people may register with the same email address for one event, with the unit (“4 people”), from Settings → “Deadlines”
tokens.gmailFallback: Only in the privacy notice: the name of the switch «Gmail takes over when Mailgun stops», quoted. Without it in the notice in force, the switch is off and messages wait for Mailgun
tokens.eventInvitations: Privacy notice only: the Invitations section's name, in quotation marks. With it in the notice in force, /admin/tasks counts the invitations as described

legal.removeBlockedReferenced: Can neither be withdrawn nor deleted permanently: {signatures}, {events} and {acknowledgements} depend on it. “Delete” on its row takes it off the list.
legal.removeBlockedCurrent: In force right now — it can neither be withdrawn nor deleted. Approve its successor first; then this one can go.
legal.deleteMeans: Deleting is permanent: the text goes entirely, and version number {version} stays retired for good.
legal.legalVersionErased: {phrase} has been deleted permanently. Its number stays retired: it will never be given to another version.

erase.title: Delete permanently: {document}, version {version}
erase.whatGoes: {document}, version {version}, in force since {date}, goes permanently: the text in both languages, the titles and the row itself. It cannot be recovered.
erase.numberRetired: Number {version} stays retired: the next version takes the next number, so a number already ticked never ends up on different words.
erase.auditOnly: Only an audit line stays: the document, the number, who approved it, the text's fingerprint and your reason. The text is not kept.
erase.nothingDepends: It can be deleted because nothing depends on it: no signature, no event, no registration — and it is not the text in force right now.
erase.termsNobodyAccepted: It can be deleted because nobody accepted it: it was in force {window}, and in that time no registration was submitted and no declaration was signed — and it is no longer the text in force.
erase.termsNeverInForce: It can be deleted because nobody accepted it: it was never the text in force.
erase.alreadyWithdrawn: You already withdrew this version, on {date}. Deleting is the second and final step: now it leaves the record as well.
erase.notWithdrawn: This version has not been withdrawn. To stop offering it, withdraw it instead: it stays on the record. Deleting cannot be undone.
erase.phraseHelp: Type exactly “{phrase}” to confirm. Anything else stops the deletion.
erase.reasonHelp: It stays in the audit log. It is the only thing that survives the deletion.
erase.blockedDraft: This is a draft, not an approved version. Delete it from the list with the button on its own row, with no typed confirmation: nobody has seen it and its number was never given to anyone.
erase.blockedCurrent: This is the version in force right now. Approve its successor first; then this one can be withdrawn or deleted.

editor.heading: Section heading
editor.imageInvalid: The address must start with https://

legal.listSocialsMissing: The notice in force does not yet describe Strava and Instagram on the public list, so they do not show. Approve a new notice from the template.
legal.listNumbersMissing: The notice in force does not yet describe the race number on the public list, so the list shows no numbers. Approve a new notice from the template.
legal.listStatesMissing: The notice in force does not yet describe the stages on the public list, so it shows only the confirmed. Approve a new notice from the template.

batch.regenerateIntro: The template changed for: {texts}. The button makes a new draft of each, with the club's facts; nothing takes effect until you approve it.
batch.regenerateBlanks: In {texts} some fields are left to fill in, written '<'…>: type them into the draft before approving.
batch.regenerateRule: Only the texts marked «New template» are regenerated; the others already have the template's words.
batch.regenerateTitle: Make new drafts from the templates ({count})?
batch.regenerateBody: A new draft is made for: {texts}. The texts in force stay as they are until you approve the drafts.
batch.upToDate: Every text already has its template's words in force, or a draft waiting to be read and approved; a new draft from the template is made once you approve or delete that one.
batch.approveBody: Approving: {versions}. From now on they are in force on the site as the club's texts; a correction is a new version.

held.superseded: a newer draft of the same text exists; delete this one or approve it from its own page.
held.behind: an approved version with a higher number is already offered, so this one would never take effect.
held.placeholders: still has fields to fill in, written '<'…>; open the draft and type them.

batch.deleteIntro: Tick the versions to delete in the table, then press the button: you see the list before anything is deleted.
batch.title: Deleting the ticked versions
batch.nothingSelected: No version is ticked. Go back to the list and tick the versions to delete.
batch.draftGoes: a draft; nobody has seen it.
batch.approvedGoes: approved; gone for good, its number stays retired.
batch.approvedConsequence: The approved versions listed ({count}) are gone for good: the text in both languages, the titles and the record. Their numbers stay retired. They cannot be recovered.
batch.phraseHelp: Type exactly "{phrase}" (the number of approved versions listed) to confirm. Anything else stops the deletion.
batch.reasonHelp: It stays in the log, on every approved version deleted. It is the only thing that survives the deletion.
batch.draftsOnly: Drafts only: nobody has seen them and their numbers were given to nobody, so no typed confirmation is asked.
batch.regenerated: Done: new drafts from the templates ({count}). Read them, then approve them.
batch.draftsApproved: Done: drafts approved ({count}), in force from now.

kinds.draftWaiting: A draft waits for approval: version {version}
kinds.templateNewHint: The text in force does not have the current template's words. Regenerate, read and approve.
kinds.regenerateBody: A new draft of {kind}, from the template, version {version}; the text in force does not change until you approve it.
kinds.unchanged: The text in force already has the template's words.
kinds.draftExists: A draft is already waiting: approve it or delete it, then you can regenerate.
kinds.blanks: The draft will still have fields to fill in, written '<'…>.

steps.title: 1. Regenerate (a draft from the template) · 2. Read the draft and fill in whatever is left written '<'…>, then “Save draft” · 3. Approve — only then is it in force
steps.body: The text in force stays on the site until you approve the draft. The four facts are the club's legal name, CIF, seat and contact address.

legal.tableCaptionOf: The versions of {kind}, with their state and what depends on each
legal.promoMissing: The notice in force does not yet describe offers and benefits, so the form does not offer the box. Approve a new notice from the template.
legal.sponsorMissing: The notice in force does not yet say the list for sponsors may be given to partners, so its button is off. Approve a new notice from the template.
legal.refusalMissing: The terms in force do not yet say on what grounds the club may refuse a registration, so the form and the registration steps do not say it. Approve new terms from the template.
legal.retireOffered: Cannot be withdrawn: {signatures}, {events} and {acknowledgements} depend on it. “Delete” takes it off the list; the text stays for whoever signed it.

tasks.howTitle: How to do it, step by step

approveLegalText.title: Approve the legal text
approveLegalText.todo: A SAMPLE, unapproved text is on the site today. Until the club approves the privacy notice, the terms and the declaration, registration refuses everyone.
approveLegalText.done: The club’s approved wording is published.
how: The short way: /admin/legal → the “One step” box → check the legal name, CIF, seat and email shown → the approval button in the box.
The notice, the terms and both race declarations, mountain event and road or park event, come into force with the club's facts in them.
To read first: on each text's card, “Regenerate from the template” → open the draft, read, fill in → “Save draft” → “Approve and publish”. All at once: “New version” → “Regenerate all”.
The long way, for a change: “New version” → pick the template → “Save draft” → PDF → “Approve and publish”. An approved text never changes; a correction is the next version.
On each event, under Registration, pick the approved declaration (if not already).

liveEmail.title: Email to real participants
liveEmail.todo: The domain {mailDomain} verified in Mailgun, then EMAIL_DELIVERY_MODE=live on production. Until then messages do not go to everyone. Mode right now
how: In Mailgun: Sending → Domains → “Add new domain”. Name: {mailDomain}. Region: EU. Not the main domain — that stays free for the club's own mailboxes.
Mailgun shows the DNS records to create: two TXT (SPF and DKIM) and one CNAME (tracking).
Add them at ROMARG → cPanel → Zone Editor exactly as Mailgun shows them, with the short name (no repeated domain).
Mind the DKIM one: the value is over 255 characters and cPanel cuts it — enter it as two quoted strings on one line (“k=rsa; p=…first part” “…the rest”), or Mailgun sees it truncated.
Then “Verify” in Mailgun — up to an hour.
Still in Mailgun: Sending → API keys → a sending key (MAILGUN_API_KEY).
Sending → Webhooks → copy the “HTTP webhook signing key” (MAILGUN_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY) and add the webhook {webhookUrl} for “Permanent Failure” and “Spam Complaints”.
The two the application acts on (a rejected address shows at the desk and on the registration). “Delivered” is optional.
In Vercel, the production project → Settings → Environment Variables (or `vercel env add NAME production`): MAILGUN_DOMAIN={mailDomain}, MAILGUN_API_KEY, MAILGUN_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY.
In the same place: MAILGUN_API_BASE_URL=https://api.eu.mailgun.net/v3 and EMAIL_REPLY_TO=a mailbox the club reads.
If no such mailbox exists yet, leave EMAIL_REPLY_TO unset: an empty one is refused at startup.
The sender is “{senderName}” <noreply@{mailDomain}> with no further setting — the name in EMAIL_FROM_NAME, the club’s own name by default.
Rehearse on QA, not on production: production refuses registrations until the legal texts are approved.
On the QA Vercel project set the same MAILGUN_DOMAIN, MAILGUN_API_KEY, MAILGUN_API_BASE_URL (the mode stays allowlist, EMAIL_ALLOWLIST=your address), redeploy, register on QA.
The email comes from noreply@{mailDomain}. When it does: on production EMAIL_DELIVERY_MODE=live, redeploy. This row turns green.

scheduler.title: Production monitors on cron-job.org
scheduler.todo: Monitors for the two scheduled jobs, with this environment's JOB_SECRET. This environment is called every {pingerDay} by day and every {pingerNight} at night. Missing or late
scheduler.done: Both jobs are running on time. This environment is called every {pingerDay} by day and every {pingerNight} at night.
how: On cron-job.org (free account): Settings → Time zone = Europe/Bucharest. Then “Create cronjob”, four times for production: two per address (one for the day, one for the night).
The addresses: {outboxUrl} and {maintenanceUrl}.

On all of them: Request method POST, and under Headers: Authorization = Bearer followed by this environment's JOB_SECRET (the value in Vercel → Settings → Environment Variables; it is not shown here).
Day: Execution schedule → Custom → every day, hours 7–22, minutes 0, 15, 30, 45 (crontab */15 7-22 * * *).
Night: Custom → every day, hours 23 and 0–6, minute 0 (0 0-6,23 * * *); the maintenance night job may skip 02:00 and 03:00 (0 0-1,4-6,23 * * *).
Turn on email notification on failure, so a dead monitor tells you. This row turns green on the first run; /devs shows each job with its last run, and the database's consumption.
At night the site answers its first request more slowly — that is intended.
On QA: the outbox every hour (0 * * * *) and maintenance every 2 hours (0 */2 * * *), and on Settings → Costs “How often the site checks” = 2 hours: QA pays for its own database's awake hours too.
The third monitor, the one that tells you when the site stops answering: “Create cronjob” with the address {baseUrl}/api/health, Request method GET, no header.
Production once an hour at minute 2 (2 0-1,4-23 * * *), QA every 6 hours (2 */6 * * *). Under Notifications tick “on failure” and “when the job gets disabled”.
The fourth, the full check, which tells you when emails stop going out: the address {baseUrl}/api/health?deep=1, daily at 04:02 (2 4 * * *), the same notifications.

retentionSweep.title: The automatic deletion of expired data is failing
retentionSweep.todo: The step that deletes data past its window failed twice in a row, so the windows no longer keep themselves. The monitors are fine
retentionSweep.done: The automatic deletion of expired data runs without errors.
how: Open /devs: the registration-maintenance row says “failing” and its last error names the steps that failed (for example “retention:registrations-after-event”).
The step names live in the retention jobs code.
In the function logs on Vercel, look for “[retention] sweep step failed”: next to the step's name is the database's error code (for example 57014, a timeout), never the values.
Fix the cause, then wait for the next run (at most 15 minutes by day, an hour at night). The row goes by itself after the first run without errors, and /api/health?deep=1 answers ok again.

inviteStaff.title: Invite the team
inviteStaff.todo: There is a single staff account — the one inserted by hand. From /admin/staff an Administrator invites organizers by email address; their Zitadel account is bound on first sign-in.
how: Open /admin/staff, type the person's email address and pick the role: Organizer (the registrations and race day) or Administrator (runs the club: the events, the registrations, the team).
Superadministrator adds the technical settings; only another Superadministrator can give this role.
“Add” emails them the club's invitation. With the invitation key set (ZITADEL_MANAGEMENT_PAT on both Vercel projects), it also creates their Zitadel account, with a password link.
They open {baseUrl}/admin, sign in through Zitadel, done. “Access Denied” means an unverified email or a different address from the invited one.

inviteKey.title: The invitation key (Zitadel)
inviteKey.todo: The key is missing (ZITADEL_MANAGEMENT_PAT). Without it, “Add” on Echipa creates no sign-in account and the person is stuck. The key is a service user's token with the Org User Manager role.
inviteKey.blind: The key authenticates but cannot create accounts: the service user is not an “Org User Manager” of the organization. The colleague added meets “User not found in the system”.
inviteKey.refused: The key is set, but Zitadel refuses the account search: the token was revoked or the account is not an “Org User Manager”. Zitadel's answer
inviteKey.unreachable: The key could not be checked: Zitadel did not answer. Not necessarily a problem with the key — reload the page in a few minutes. The answer
inviteKey.done: The key works: checked just now with a real search, it found your account. “Add” on Echipa creates the sign-in account and Zitadel sends the password link.
how: Zitadel console → Users → Service Accounts → New: user name “brasovrunners-invites”, name “{club} — invitații”, access token type Bearer. Create.
Organization → Managers → + New: the service account, role Org User Manager. The dialog is called “Add an Administrator”; if it asks for a Loginname, that is “brasovrunners-invites”.
Not “Role Assignments”.
On the service account → Personal Access Tokens → New.
The console offers no expiry here and the token does not expire — it is a secret that has to be revoked by hand, on the same screen, when it is no longer wanted.
Copy it (shown once) into the password manager and note there that it has no end date.
Vercel → the production project → Settings → Environment Variables: ZITADEL_MANAGEMENT_PAT = the token (Production). The same on the QA project. Redeploy both.
Check: reload this page after the redeploy — the row turns green when the key finds your account, without inviting anybody.
Then, on Echipa, “Add” creates the account and Zitadel sends the password link; whoever has not signed in yet has “Resend the invitation” on their row.
howBroken: Zitadel console → Organization → Managers → + New: the key's service account (“brasovrunners-invites”), role Org User Manager. The dialog is called “Add an Administrator”.
Not “Role Assignments”: that page grants roles inside a project and does not help create users.
If Zitadel answered 401 or the token was revoked: on the service account → Personal Access Tokens → New, then the new token as ZITADEL_MANAGEMENT_PAT on both Vercel projects and redeploy.
Check: reload this page; the row turns green when the key finds your account.
Then, on Echipa, for every colleague marked “No sign-in account”: ⋮ → “Revoke access”, then “Add” again with the same address.
howUnreachable: Reload the page in a few minutes: the check runs on every open, with one search in Zitadel.
If it stays so, open the Zitadel console. If it does not open, the provider has a problem; if it does, check ZITADEL_MANAGEMENT_PAT and AUTH_ZITADEL_ISSUER on Vercel.
inviteKey.capped: The organization has more accounts than the check reads: at most 2000, 200 to a page. The key may well work, but Echipa can no longer say which row has no sign-in account.
howCapped: Nothing to fix on the key.
A developer raises the ACCOUNTS_LISTING_MAX ceiling in the Zitadel accounts code, or deletes the accounts no longer used in the Zitadel console.

mediaStorage.title: Photo storage (Cloudflare R2)
mediaStorage.todo: The gallery needs somewhere to put photos. Until then, albums can be created but cannot receive photos.
how: A Cloudflare account (free) on the club's address. The domain does not move there.
Left menu → R2 Object Storage → enable R2 (this is where the card is asked for; nothing is charged under 10 GB).
Create bucket → name “brasovrunners-media”, location “European Union”.
Then, in the bucket's settings, enable “Public access” through the r2.dev subdomain (or a custom domain) and copy the public address — that is R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL.
R2 → “Manage R2 API Tokens” → Create API token → name “brasovrunners-site”, permission “Object Read & Write”, this bucket only.
Copy the Access Key ID, the Secret Access Key and the S3 endpoint (shown once).
In Vercel → the production project (and QA) → Settings → Environment Variables: R2_ENDPOINT, R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID, R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, R2_BUCKET=brasovrunners-media, R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL. Redeploy.
This row turns green and the album page gets its upload button.

publishEvents.title: Publish events
publishEvents.todo: No event is published, so visitors see an empty list.
how: Open /admin/events → “New event”. Fill in the type, the date, the place and the title in both languages. Save.
Press “Publish” — a draft goes live in one press. Both languages go live together; until then the page is a 404 for visitors.
Only one event can be “featured” — it opens the home page. Next year: “Duplicate” this year's.

raceDaySheets.title: Delete the event's exports and printed sheets
raceDaySheets.todo: Seven days have passed since the event: destroy the downloaded lists and printed sheets, within 30 days at the latest. The row goes by itself.
raceDaySheets.done: No list or sheet to destroy right now.
how: Delete the CSV and xlsx files downloaded for the event and the all-declarations PDF — from Downloads, from the bin, and from any email or chat you sent them through.
If a list must be kept, cut the identity document column first.
On declarations signed on paper, cross out or cover the identity document's series and number. The paper stays three years, then it is destroyed too.
Destroy the emergency sheet and any other list printed for race day (shredder, or torn small).
In the club's Gmail, delete the race declaration copies older than three years. Where a subject comes in either language, the search carries both, so it finds it.
Search subject:("Declarație semnată" OR "Signed declaration") -subject:("Declarație semnată (alergare de grup)" OR "Signed declaration (group run)") older_than:3y, then delete everything it finds.
Group-run copies are not deleted by age: they stay while the declaration is active, as each one's email says. The search above leaves them out.
Delete the contact-form messages older than 12 months: search subject:"Mesaj de pe site" older_than:1y, then delete everything it finds.
In the same place, delete the confirmation notices sent to the club and the club copies of participants' emails, older than three years.
Search subject:("Înscriere confirmată" OR "Registration confirmed" OR "Copie club" OR "Club copy") older_than:3y, then delete everything it finds.

botCheck.title: The anti-bot check on registration (Cloudflare Turnstile)
botCheck.todo: The widget “brasovrunners-site” exists and both keys are on both Vercel projects; this row turns green on the next deployment. Turnstile stops the bots the form's trap field does not catch.
botCheck.done: The registration form has the anti-bot check on.
botCheck.misconfigured: Both keys are set, but Cloudflare says the secret key is wrong. Nobody is refused because of it, but the bot defence is weaker until you fix the key below.
how: ✓ Cloudflare (the same account as for the photos) → left menu → Turnstile → Add widget.
✓ Name “brasovrunners-site”; hostnames: the club's domain and the qa subdomain; Widget mode “Managed”. Save: you get a Site key and a Secret key.
✓ In Vercel → the production project (and QA, same keys) → Settings → Environment Variables: TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY and TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY. Redeploy.
✓ Open the registration form: the “Verify you are human” box appears under the fields; a test registration goes through. This row turns green.
howMisconfigured: Cloudflare → Turnstile → the “brasovrunners-site” widget → copy the Secret key again; if it may have leaked, press Rotate Secret Key.
Vercel → the production project → Settings → Environment Variables: replace TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY, then Redeploy. The same on QA, if it has its own key.
Reload this page after the deployment: the row turns green once Cloudflare accepts the secret again. A test registration is not required — this row is checked without one.

declarationArchiveMail.todo: When DECLARATIONS_ARCHIVE_TO is set, every signed declaration, online or on paper, also reaches the club's mailbox as an attachment. One more message per registration on the 100 a day.
declarationArchiveMail.done: Every signed declaration also reaches the club's archive mailbox automatically.

vercelUsage.title: Vercel usage in figures, on /devs
vercelUsage.todo: With a read token and the project id, /devs shows the month's deployments, today's out of 100 a day and the build minutes out of 6,000 a month. Traffic is only in Vercel → Usage.
vercelUsage.done: /devs shows the month's deployments and build minutes, with a warning threshold.
how: Vercel → avatar → Account Settings → Tokens → Create: name “brasovrunners-devs”, scope your account, expiry 1 year. Copy the token (shown once).
The project id: Vercel → the production project → Settings → General → Project ID (starts with prj_).

contactForm.title: The contact form
contactForm.todo: Messages from “Write to us” reach the club through Gmail. Until the account is configured, the page shows the club's address instead of the form.
contactForm.done: The contact form sends to the club's mailbox.
how: The club's Google account → Security → 2-Step Verification: on (without it Google gives no app passwords).

Open {baseUrl}/en/contact and send a test message: “Your message is on its way.” on the page and the email in the mailbox, with “Reply” addressed to whoever wrote. This row turns green.

neonLimits.title: The database's monthly compute-time limit
neonLimits.todo: No monthly limit is set on this environment, or it could not be read from Neon: nothing caps the Neon bill. Set one under Costs → “The database's limits”.
neonLimits.broken: 80% or more of the monthly limit is already spent. At the limit, Neon stops the database until next month: raise the limit today.
neonLimits.done: A monthly limit is set on this environment, and this period is comfortably under it.
how: On the Costs tab, open “The database's limits”, choose “With a limit” and type the number recommended there.
That key is enough when it is project-scoped: Neon gives such a key Editor access to its project, which reads and writes the limits.
If Neon refuses the write, the card says so and names the key that would do.
Check: after saving, the readout above the form is what Neon now holds, never what was sent. This row turns green under 80% of the limit, and red at or past it.

refusalTerms.title: Terms: the club's right to refuse a registration
refusalTerms.todo: The terms in force do not yet say on what grounds the club may refuse a registration, so the form's box and the registration steps say nothing of it until the club approves terms from the template.
refusalTerms.done: The terms in force state the grounds: the form's box also names the club refusing or cancelling a registration, and the registration steps say the club may refuse only on an objective ground.
how: /admin/legal → the “Terms” card (it says «New template») → “Regenerate from the template” → confirm. Section 3 states the grounds on which the club may refuse a registration.
A lawyer reads the last paragraph of section 3 first. Then open the draft, fill in what is left, “Save draft”, then “Approve and publish”.
Once in force, in both languages, the form's box and the registration steps state the club's right to refuse, with no other setting.

listStatesNotice.title: Privacy notice: the stages on the public list
listStatesNotice.todo: The notice in force does not describe the stages of the public participant list yet, so the list shows only confirmed participants, until the club approves a notice that does.
listStatesNotice.done: The notice in force describes the stages: beside each name, confirmed or registered awaiting confirmation; “on the waiting list” only where the event has «The waiting list is public».
how: /admin/legal → the “GDPR” card → “Regenerate from the template” → confirm. The section on the public list describes the stages.
Open the draft, read it, fill in what is left, “Save draft”, then “Approve and publish”. Once it takes effect, every public list that is switched on shows the stages.
Approve the terms and the declaration from their templates as well, if not already, so they all say the same.

listSocialsNotice.title: Privacy notice: Strava and Instagram on the public list
listSocialsNotice.todo: The notice in force does not yet describe Strava and Instagram on the public list, so they show for nobody until the club approves a new notice.
listSocialsNotice.done: The notice in force describes Strava and Instagram on the public list: the form offers the tick, and the list shows them beside the names of those who ticked it.
how: /admin/legal → the “GDPR” card → “Regenerate from the template” → confirm. The section on the public list describes Strava and Instagram beside a name.
Open the draft, read it, fill in what is left, “Save draft”, then “Approve and publish”.
From the moment it takes effect, the form offers the tick, with no other setting; the list shows them only for those who register from then on and tick it.
Approve the terms from the template as well, if not already, so they say the same about the list.

listNumbersNotice.done: The notice in force describes the race number: the list shows it in a “BIB” column for every confirmed runner who has one; those without show “—”.
how: Before approving, write to the registered: /admin/events → event → “Send a message to participants”. Say their number will appear beside their name in “Who's coming” and how to withdraw (next step).
Withdrawing: in “My registrations” (or the link in the email) press “I do not want to appear on the participants & results list”; the number leaves with the name.
/admin/legal → the “GDPR” card → “Regenerate from the template” → confirm. The section on the public list describes the race number beside the names of the confirmed.
Open the draft, read it, fill in what is left, “Save draft”, then “Approve and publish”.
From then on, the list shows the “BIB” column for every confirmed runner who has a number, whichever notice they registered under.
Approve the terms from the template as well, if not already, so they say the same about the list.

newsletterNotice.title: Privacy notice: the newsletter
newsletterNotice.todo: The notice in force does not describe the newsletter yet, so the contact page offers no news subscription and we keep no address for it, until the club approves a notice that describes it.
newsletterNotice.done: The notice in force describes the newsletter: the contact page offers the subscription, with the topics chosen and a confirmation by email.
how: /admin/legal → the “GDPR” card → “Regenerate from the template” → confirm. Section 5 has the paragraph about the club's news, and section 7 how long the address is kept.
Open the draft, read it, fill in what is left, “Save draft”, then “Approve and publish”. Once in force in both languages, the contact page shows “Subscribe to the news”, with no other setting.
You write the newsletter from the backoffice's “Newsletter” menu; the new-event announcements go by themselves.

teamPageNotice.title: Privacy notice: the team page
teamPageNotice.todo: The notice in force does not yet describe the team page, which shows the names and photographs of the club's team and volunteers. Approve a new notice before publishing the page.
teamPageNotice.done: The notice in force describes the team page: what it shows, on what basis, and how a card is taken down.
how: /admin/legal → the “GDPR” card → “Regenerate from the template” → confirm. Section 4 describes the team page.
Open the draft, read it, fill in what is left, “Save draft”, then “Approve and publish”. The row closes by itself once the notice takes effect.
Only then publish the page, from /admin/pages/team → “Publish the page”.
The same new notice also describes, in section 12, the club members' accounts (the members' area): approve it before inviting the first members from Team → “Add several members”.

translation.title: Automatic translation from Romanian (DeepL, free)
translation.todo: The “Copy and translate everything: RO → EN” and “Translate from Romanian” buttons start once the DeepL key is on the server; until then, the English is written by hand.
translation.done: Automatic translation is on: at the top of every editor, "Copy and translate everything: RO → EN" translates it all in one press.
how: Create a DeepL API account (the "DeepL API" page on DeepL's site): one key, with a one-time credit of 1,000,000 characters that does not renew monthly.
DeepL may ask for a card for verification only; the credit is not charged, and a paid plan is chosen only with the club's explicit yes.
In the DeepL account → API Keys: copy the key (a free one ends in ":fx").
In Vercel → the production project (and QA, with the same key or its own) → Settings → Environment Variables: DEEPL_API_KEY = the key. TRANSLATE_PROVIDER need not be set: it defaults to deepl.
Redeploy.
Open an event: at the top, "Copy and translate everything: RO → EN" is no longer grey, and "Translate from Romanian" shows under the English boxes. This row turns green.
The daily budget is chosen under Settings → Costs.
translation.credit: Automatic translation is on: at the top of every editor, "Copy and translate everything: RO → EN" translates it all in one press. The DeepL credit: {creditUsed} of {creditLimit} characters used ({creditPercent}), {creditRemaining} left — given once.
translation.creditUnread: Automatic translation is on. The DeepL credit: — {creditReason}
translation.watch: Over 80% of the DeepL credit is used: {creditUsed} of {creditLimit} characters ({creditPercent}), {creditRemaining} left. It does not come back next month.
translation.low: The DeepL credit is nearly spent: {creditUsed} of {creditLimit} characters ({creditPercent}), {creditRemaining} left. Get a new credit or key ready.
translation.spent: The DeepL credit is spent ({creditUsed} of {creditLimit} characters): translation is stopped. A new credit or key is needed.
howCredit: Sign in to the DeepL account, on the "DeepL API" page of DeepL's site → Usage: see what is left of the credit — the same figure as under Settings → Costs.
Choose: a new key, with its one-time credit of 1,000,000 characters that does not renew — or a paid plan, only with the club's explicit yes, since the club uses free plans.
In Vercel → the production project (and QA) → Settings → Environment Variables: DEEPL_API_KEY = the new key. Redeploy.
Within an hour (or at the first translation), Settings → Costs shows the new credit, and this row turns green.

raceDeclarations.title: The race declarations: mountain event, and road or park event
raceDeclarations.todo: One of the two race declarations has no version from the template yet. Until the road one is approved, asphalt races sign the mountain event one.
raceDeclarations.done: Both race declarations, mountain event and road or park event, are in force from the template: every race signs the declaration that fits its course.
how: /admin/legal → the “Self-declaration — mountain event” card → “Regenerate from the template”. Then the draft: read, fill in, “Save draft”, then “Approve and publish”.
The same for “Self-declaration — road / park event”.
A new race starts on the kind that fits its course by itself. A race saved earlier keeps the declaration chosen then.
An asphalt race on the mountain event one: open it, and the “Self-declaration” card says when the kind does not fit the course. Choose the road or park one and save.

groupRunSeriesTexts.title: The group-run declarations: one signature per series
groupRunSeriesTexts.todo: The group-run declarations in force cover one date, so a runner signs again on each date. The new template covers the whole series (or the one-day run); approve it.
groupRunSeriesTexts.done: The group-run declarations in force say what they cover: a runner signs once for the whole series.
how: /admin/legal → the “Self-declaration (group run, asphalt)” card → “Regenerate from the template”. Then the draft: read, fill in, “Save draft”, then “Approve and publish”.
The same for “Self-declaration (group run, trail)”.
Approve a new version of the privacy notice from the template too: it says a series' declaration is kept while it is active, and after a withdrawal for at most three years.
Whoever signed the old version sees on the run's page, from the link in their email, that the new version is asked for; the old signature stays in the list.

promoNotice.title: Privacy notice: offers and benefits
promoNotice.todo: The notice in force does not yet describe offers and benefits, so the form does not offer the box and no consent is kept until the club approves a new notice.
promoNotice.done: The notice in force describes offers and benefits: the form offers the box, and everyone changes their answer from their registration's page.
how: /admin/legal → the “GDPR” card → “Regenerate from the template” → confirm. Section 5 describes the offers and benefits from the club and its partners.
Open the draft, read it, fill in what is left, “Save draft”, then “Approve and publish”.
From the moment it takes effect, the form offers the box, with no other setting. Whoever ticks it appears in «Newsletter», in its own card.

sponsorNotice.title: Privacy notice: the list for sponsors
sponsorNotice.todo: The notice in force does not yet say that partners may receive the first name, last name and address of those who ticked offers and benefits, so «Download the list for sponsors» is off.
sponsorNotice.done: The notice in force says the list may be given to partners: «Download the list for sponsors» is on and takes only the consents given under it.
how: /admin/legal → the “GDPR” card → “Regenerate from the template” → confirm. Sections 5 and 6 say partners may receive the first name, last name and address.
Open the draft, read it, fill in what is left, “Save draft”, then “Approve and publish”.
The list takes only the consents given under the new notice. Whoever ticked under an older notice never reaches a partner.

gmailFallbackNotice.title: Privacy notice: Gmail takes over when Mailgun stops
gmailFallbackNotice.todo: The notice in force does not yet say a message may leave through Gmail while Mailgun is stopped: «Gmail takes over when Mailgun stops» stays off, and emails wait for Mailgun.
gmailFallbackNotice.done: The notice in force says a message may leave through Gmail while Mailgun is stopped: «Gmail takes over when Mailgun stops» works, as the Administrator leaves it.
how: /admin/legal → the “GDPR” card → “Regenerate from the template” → confirm. Section 6 says a message may leave through the club's Gmail (Google) when Mailgun refuses or delays.
Open the draft, read it, fill in what is left, “Save draft”, then “Approve and publish”.
Why: a participant's name, links and signed PDF then reach Google, and the notice has to say so first. Once it is approved the switch is no longer grey.

emailFailSafe.title: Emails nothing is carrying
emailFailSafe.todo: Mailgun said stop over 90 minutes ago and nothing carries the emails, an email is still refused for now after six attempts, or one failed in the last 7 days.
emailFailSafe.broken: Mailgun said stop over 90 minutes ago and nothing carries the emails, an email is still refused for now after six attempts, or one failed in 7 days. Nothing is lost.
emailFailSafe.done: No email stuck or failed. If Mailgun says stop, Gmail takes over (when the switch is on).
how: «Settings» → «Emails» → «How emails leave» → «Gmail takes over when Mailgun stops»: Yes → «Save the routes». While Mailgun is paused or out of allowance, Gmail carries every group.
If Gmail has reached its limit: in the same place, «Gmail limit per day» above it (500 at most, and the club's people also send by hand from that account).
The failed emails: «Settings» → «Emails» → «The sending queue» → «Retry the failed emails». It puts them back in the queue, from the first attempt.
An email refused for now (5xx, 404) is retried on its own every hour; its reason is on its row in the queue. A 404 that does not pass: check MAILGUN_API_BASE_URL and MAILGUN_DOMAIN on Vercel.
If Mailgun asked for the pause for the pace (the probation): «Settings» → «Emails» → the Mailgun plan → «Hourly limit» — 90 while the probation lasts.
The queue's header says until when Mailgun is stopped and who takes over.

invitationsNotice.todo: The notice in force does not yet describe invitations by email. The club may send invitations now; the notice must say what data it keeps for them.
invitationsNotice.done: The notice in force describes the invitations: the invited person's name and address, the basis and how long they are kept.
how: /admin/legal → the “GDPR” card → “Regenerate from the template” → confirm. Section 2 describes the invitations.
Open the draft, read it, fill in what is left, “Save draft”, then “Approve and publish”. The row closes by itself once the notice takes effect.

freeVerdict.freeExceptDomain: Yes, apart from the domain: every service is on a free plan and nothing is paid monthly.
freeVerdict.paysForUsage: Almost: the domain and the database are paid for (Neon Launch, by usage), and every other service is on a free plan.
freeVerdict.paysForPlans: Paid for: {services}; every other service is on a free plan.
freeVerdict.freeButAtALimit: Yes, but today's free emails are used up, and the rest go out after midnight.
freeVerdict.notFree: Careful: a published event charges a fee, and the free plans do not care that we are a non-profit.
freeVerdict.paysForUsageMore: Launch has no subscription and was chosen by the club on 22 September 2026.
freeVerdict.freeButAtALimitMore: Nothing is lost. If you open entries now, the confirmations arrive tomorrow morning.
freeVerdict.notFreeMore: Not necessarily a problem: a donation is allowed, a compulsory fee is not, even if it only covers costs.

nextSpend.vercelMore: It arrives only if the site starts asking for money to take part, or if the site's code moves to the club's own account.

freshness.stale: Prices were checked on {checked}, {days} days ago: ask the developer to check them before any decision.

tasks.servicesTitle: The services, one at a time
tasks.servicesIntro: One row for each service the site depends on.

domain.name: The site's address (the .com domain)
domain.freeGives: There is no free version: this is the one thing on the page that is paid for.
domain.ceiling: No ceiling: one invoice a year for the .com, in lei.
domain.whenCrossed: The next step is renewing the .com for several years.
domain.closeYes: This deployment answers on the club's domain.
domain.closeNo: This deployment answers on the provider's address — for QA or a laptop, that is as it should be.
domain.more: Bought on 16 September 2026 from ROMARG, for a year; ROMARG invoices in lei, with VAT. The .ro is no longer bought.

mailgun.name: Mailgun (sending email)
mailgun.freeGives: Free: 100 emails a day, on one account used by both QA and production.
mailgun.ceiling: The first limit: 100 emails a day, about 33 entries at three emails each.
mailgun.whenCrossed: Emails over the limit go out after midnight, so the paid plan is bought before entries open.
mailgun.closeMeasured: {used} of {of} emails have gone out today, enough for about {left} entries.
mailgun.bumpBack: Taken for the month of the race and stopped the month after, not as a subscription.
mailgun.closeMeasuredMonth: This month {used} of {of} emails went out (plan {plan}), enough for about {left} more registrations.
mailgun.more: QA and production share the allowance. Emails over it are not lost, but they leave only the next day.

vercel.name: Vercel (where the site lives)
vercel.freeGives: Free: enough traffic and power for a club site, but only for non-commercial use.
vercel.ceiling: The first limit: the site may not be used commercially, and the club sells nothing, so we are fine.
vercel.whenCrossed: A compulsory fee for an event would count as commercial; a donation would not.
vercel.closeYes: A published event is marked as charging a fee — check how it is worded.
vercel.closeNo: No published event asks for money.
vercel.bumpBack: This one does not come back down: it is a change in how the site is used, not a busy weekend.
vercel.more: Over a free-plan limit, the feature stops for 30 days and no payment restarts it: move up before a race, not during one.

pro.freeGives: Pro: {seats} at {seatPrice} USD a month each, with {credit} USD of usage included.
pro.ceiling: No limit measured here: the usage credit is on the Vercel dashboard.
pro.whenCrossed: Usage beyond the credit is billed on top, on the same invoice.
pro.bumpBack: Taken for the race's months and can be given back after it; the card's note says when and why.
pro.more: Pro is taken so the site's functions do not stop before the race; the card's note says when it was taken.
pro.close: On Pro, the “non-commercial only” rule no longer applies.

neon.name: Neon (the database)
neon.freeGives: Free: a small database (half a gigabyte) and an amount of work included every month.
neon.ceiling: The first limit: the space and the monthly amount of work included.
neon.whenCrossed: Past the limit the site gets slow and errors can appear.
neon.closeMeasured: Measured from the database: {used} MB of {of} MB used.
neon.closeUnknown: Not measured: the site does not know how much has been used; it is in the Neon account.
neon.closeNo: No ceiling on Launch: what is used is what is paid.
neon.bumpBack: Taken for the days entries are open and dropped once they close.

launch.freeGives: Launch: paid by usage, no subscription, at the plan's rates.
launch.ceiling: No ceiling: nothing stops when usage grows — the bill grows.
launch.whenCrossed: The bill stays small only while the database sleeps after five minutes without a request.
launch.close: This month, at the pace so far ({cu} CU-hours, about {perDay} a day): about ${usd} a month, an estimate.
launch.closeUnknown: The month's pace appears once NEON_API_KEY is set; until then the figure is in the Neon console → Billing.
launch.bumpBack: The way back is the December 2026 review: one choice under “The Neon plan”, no deployment.
launch.closeMore: At ${rate}/CU-hour and ${storageRate}/GB-month; the invoice is Neon's.
launch.more: The monitors wake the database every 15 minutes by day and hourly at night; more often would keep it awake and paid. In December the club may go back to Free.

neon.monthly: Compute hours (CU) are on /devs. Monthly cost if we left Free, at this month's pace ({cu} CU-hours so far): about ${usd}/month on Launch (${rate}/CU-hour, ${storageRate}/GB, no subscription).
neon.monthlyUnknown: Compute hours (CU) are on /devs. Monthly cost on Launch: ${rate}/CU-hour + ${storageRate}/GB, no subscription; the exact pace appears once NEON_API_KEY is set.
neon.more: On the free plan the database sleeps when unused, so the first page after a quiet spell is slower. The next step up is paid by usage.

zitadel.name: Zitadel (sign-in for the team and members)
zitadel.freeGives: Free: up to 100 daily active users, any number of stored users — the club's members fit —, unlimited organizations, 3 identity providers. Checked on 27 Sept 2026.
zitadel.ceiling: The one limit that matters: a single administrator, without whom nobody can invite anybody.
zitadel.whenCrossed: It is not crossed: who the administrator is and where the credentials are is written down.
zitadel.closeNo: The team signs in on the provider's address, as decided.
zitadel.more: Signing in happens on the provider's address, not the club's: a login address of our own would cost 100 USD a month.

scheduler.name: cron-job.org + GitHub (the automatic jobs)
scheduler.freeGives: Both free: cron-job.org calls the jobs every 15 minutes, which is what sends the emails, and GitHub Actions is the safety net.
scheduler.ceiling: Here the limit is rhythm: without the cron-job.org monitors the jobs only run from the safety net, roughly every two hours.
scheduler.whenCrossed: Email waits in the queue, and places held for somebody are released later than they should be.
scheduler.closeYes: An automatic job has not run for too long.
scheduler.closeNo: The automatic jobs ran on time.
scheduler.more: Email goes out right after each registration regardless. Nothing breaks and nobody loses their place, but the confirmation arrives late, and on registration day that feels like a broken site.

tasks.decisionsTitle: What is waiting on a decision
tasks.decisionsIntro: The rest of this page is things to read. These are only the questions still without an answer, each with somebody in particular who has to give it.

entryContribution.question: Will the club ever ask for money to take part?
entryContribution.open: A published event charges a fee. Decide whether it is a donation or a compulsory fee before it takes entries: free hosting depends on it.
entryContribution.answered: No. The club sells nothing and takes no money. If that changes: a donation is allowed on the free plan, a compulsory fee is not.

mailgunBeforeRace.question: Do we take a paid month of Mailgun before the first real race?
mailgunBeforeRace.open: The free allowance covers about 33 entries a day. If you expect more, pay the $15 the day before entries open.
mailgunBeforeRace.answered: The club no longer depends on the free daily limit.

jobCadence.title: How often the site checks
jobCadence.intro: How often the two scheduled jobs may wake the database.

inForce.onDemand: In force: on demand (default) — only when something is due, and in any case once a day, at {time}.
inForce.every: In force: at most once every {minutes} min, for each job.

jobCadence.cost: What a longer interval costs: a waiting-list offer, a reminder, an announcement or a race number may go out up to that many minutes late.
jobCadence.safe: What does not change: a held place still lapses on time.
jobCadence.onTheHour: The safety check happens once a day, at {time}, together with the monitor's full check (/api/health?deep=1).
jobCadence.lastPingSkipped: last ping: {when}, skipped without the database
jobCadence.readOnly: The Superadministrator changes the interval, because a wrong one delays every job.
jobCadence.fieldHelp: "On demand" means only when something is due, plus the daily safety check at {time}.

option.onDemand: On demand (default) — when something is due, and once a day at {time}

jobCadence.saved: The interval was saved and applies from the next ping.

emails.immediate: Emails go out right after the request that queued them, whatever the interval.
emails.scheduled: Emails now go out only when the scheduled queue runs («Deadlines» → «When emails leave»), so the interval delays them too.
emails.immediateMore: The scheduled queue only picks up what is left: a retry, or a message deferred until the daily allowance resets.
emails.scheduledMore: The club's sending setting is on “scheduled”; the delay is up to as many minutes as the interval.

jobCadence.introMore: The jobs are registration maintenance and the email outbox. With nothing to do they do not wake the database; every wake-up costs at least 5 minutes of compute.
jobCadence.safeMore: Every reading of the places counts the deadlines at that moment, whether or not the job has run. Your setting wins.
jobCadence.onTheHourMore: A day with nothing to do costs one wake of the database, at {time}. A deadline (a held place, a reminder) keeps its own time. With an interval chosen, some may be up to a quarter of an hour late.
jobCadence.fieldHelpMore: A ping inside the interval answers from the cache, without the database, exactly like one with nothing to do.

budgetThresholds.saved: The thresholds are saved; the month's budget is read by them from now on.

desk.title: Number pickup desk
desk.howTitle: How race day works, step by step
how: Before the race (organizer): on the event page, under “Taking part and registration” → “Allocate and print”, press “Download every number (PDF)” and print them — two to an A4 sheet.
Print a few “Paper declaration form (PDF)” too, for anyone who signs on the spot.
An administrator prints blank numbers from “Spare bibs for on-the-spot entries” for people who register at the desk.
Volunteers: an Administrator makes their accounts from “Staff”, with the Volunteer role. With their account they open this page on their phone. That is all they see: name, state, number.
No email addresses, and nobody can be cancelled from here.
Every confirmed participant got a QR code by email. At the desk: press “Scan” (on Android) or open the phone's camera and point it at the code — the person's row opens.
Or search by name or by race number.
Press “Mark present” and hand over the number from the pile. No number? Type it in the box and press “Save no.”.
No email arrived, or they cannot find the QR: search by name.
If it says “Așteaptă semnarea declarației” (awaiting the declaration), give them the paper declaration to sign, press “Confirm on paper”, then “Mark present”.
Never registered at all: “Add somebody”. Name and email.
The “This person is at the desk” tick is already set, and “Number given now” suggests the next spare number: hand them that bib and write their name on it in marker.
They sign the paper declaration, then “Mark present”. If the event is full they join the waiting list; “Give a place” only works once one is free.
Made a mistake? “Undo” takes it back. Every press stays in the registration's history, with your name on it.
At the end, the figures on this page are the race's figures: how many confirmed, how many here. Whoever did not come stays without “here”.
A red box saying “Registration cancelled” or “expired”? The person no longer has a place, even with the email in hand: no number, no check-in.
If it says the number was printed, pull that bib out of the pile — numbers are never reused.

when.WAITLIST_JOINED: After the address is confirmed, when the event is full.
when.WAITLIST_SPOT_OFFER: When a place frees and this person is first in line. {offer} to sign.
when.REGISTRATION_CONFIRMED: After the declaration is signed — or at the desk, on paper.
when.REGISTRATION_CANCELLED: When the participant withdraws or an organizer cancels the registration.
when.WAITLIST_OFFER_EXPIRED: Not sent any more: when an offered place's {offer} pass without a signature, the place moves to the next person in line with no email to the one who did not sign.
when.REGISTRATION_MANAGE_LINK: Not sent any more: “Resend the link” sends the whole confirmation, with the manage link, the QR code and the number; “My registrations” has its own message.
when.PROFILE_MANAGE_LINK: On request, when somebody wants to see all their registrations.
when.REGISTRATION_STATE_NOTICE: Resent by an organizer when somebody asks where they stand.
when.EVENT_REMINDER: Automatic, {reminder} before the start (or as the event chooses), to everyone confirmed, once. Scheduled events only: a cancelled one sends nothing automatic any more.
when.EVENT_THANKS: By hand, from the event page, once the start time has passed; once, to those checked in at the desk. Never for a cancelled event.
when.DECLARATION_SIGNED: Not sent any more: the signed declaration, as a PDF, goes attached to “Registration confirmed”, together with a link to it.
when.DECLARATION_ARCHIVE: With the signed declaration, to the club's declarations mailbox, for real registrations only. The identity document is masked.
when.BIB_ASSIGNED: When someone sets a confirmed registration's number by hand. With the QR code.
when.STAFF_INVITATION: When an administrator adds somebody on Echipa, and on "Resend the invitation" while that person has not signed in yet. To the colleague's address, no token: the sign-in page decides who they are.
when.REGISTRATION_OPENED: When registration opens, once, to every address left at “Tell me” on the event's page.
when.CLUB_CONFIRMATION_NOTICE: On every confirmation of a real registration, to the club addresses above. No action link and no token.
when.EVENT_UPDATE_NOTICE: Only when the organizer ticks “Tell the participants” on saving and the place, date, time or programme changed, or they wrote a note. To every active registration.
when.EVENT_CANCELLED: When an organizer cancels the event with “Tell the participants” ticked: their reason, to every active registration. The registrations are not cancelled.
when.ORGANIZER_MESSAGE: When an organizer sends a message from the event's page → “Send a message to participants”, to the group chosen. The preview uses a sample text.
when.GROUP_RUN_DECLARATION_SIGNED: After someone signs a group run's optional declaration, to the address they gave — and again if they sign once more on another date of the same run. With the declaration as a PDF.
when.GROUP_RUN_DECLARATION_ARCHIVE: With a declaration signed on a group run, to the club's declarations mailbox. The identity document is masked.
when.REGISTER_ANOTHER_PERSON: When the form is sent again with an address already registered and another name: a single-use link, valid for {confirmation}, to register the other person.
when.NEWSLETTER_CONFIRM: When someone subscribes on the contact page: the link that confirms the subscription, valid for {confirmation}.
when.NEWSLETTER: Only when an organizer sends a newsletter from the backoffice, to the chosen topic's subscribers. It leaves after every other email, from what is left of the allowance.
when.NEW_EVENT_ALERT: Once for each new event published (never the weekly run), to those subscribed to new events and to its topics.

retryFailed.done: Failed emails put back in the queue: {count}.

status.month: Plan {plan}: {sent} of {allowance} messages sent this month, {remaining} left; no daily limit; waiting: {waiting}.
status.none: Plan {plan}: no limit. Sent today: {sent}; waiting: {waiting}.

links.label: Action links

confirmations.label: Confirmations and status changes

reminders.label: Reminders and thank-yous

guide.title: User guide
guide.intro: Every task has its numbered steps; the words «like this», in bold, are exactly what the button says. If a button is missing, you do not have the role for it.

sections.title: First steps
sections.who: For everyone: sign in, find your way, confirm what you press.

tasks.title: Sign in to the backoffice
steps: The first time: open the invitation email the club sent you and choose your password from it.
Open the club's site and add /en/admin at the end of the address.
On the «Staff sign-in» page press «Sign in» and use the email address the invitation came to and your password.
The top says «Signed in as» with your name and role. If the role is not the one you expected, tell an administrator.
On a computer that is not yours, press «Sign out» when you finish.

tasks.title: The top bar: what each tab holds
steps: You see only your role's tabs; the rest do not exist for you, and that is fine.
«Events»: opens on the upcoming ones; under «State» choose «All» or another. «New event» and «Edit» are here; a role that only reads sees «Open».
«Registrations»: who signed up, with filters, the export and each registration's page.
«Race day»: the number pickup desk, on a phone.
«Gallery» and «Pages» (the standard pages — «Contact», «The team», «FAQ», «Members» — and the club's own pages).

«Settings»: «Emails» (what participants receive, the Mailgun plan, the hourly limit, the Gmail routes, the sending queue), «Deadlines», «Appearance», «Costs», «Anti-bot» and, at the end of the row, «Configuration» (for the Technical role and the Administrators).

«Tasks» → «Club»: what the club still has to do, read from the system, with the steps under each row. «Tasks» → «To do»: the club's list, typed and ticked by hand — add a line, give it to somebody, set a due day, tick it when it is done.
«Legal documents»: the terms, the privacy notice (GDPR) and the declarations.
«Staff» and «Guide» (this page).

tasks.title: The question before an important press
steps: Whatever publishes, cancels, erases or sends emails asks first, in a window. Read it: it says what happens and how many participants get an email.
To go ahead, press the button with the same name in the window. To stop, «Never mind».
Once it worked, a message at the bottom says for a few seconds what was done.
If something is missing, a red box at the top names each gap as a link: tap it, fill it in, press again. What you typed stays.

tasks.title: What each role can do
steps: The Volunteer: the race-day desk — finds a runner, confirms on the paper declaration the participant signed, gives a free place, a number, checks people in. Sees a name, a state and a number, never an email address.
The Redactor: the events' texts and the site's pages, in both languages. Does not change an event's settings and does not publish.
The Organizer: reads the events, every registration, the export and the race numbers; messages participants; works the desk. Does not change an event, cancel or erase a registration.
The Tehnic role: the site's configuration page, for troubleshooting. Does not change events and does not see the registrations.

The Administrator runs the club: everything the Organizer and the Redactor do, plus the events («New event», «Edit», «Create and publish»), correcting, cancelling and erasing a registration, resending emails, «Assign numbers», «Deadlines», the Mailgun plan, the legal documents (new version, approval, withdrawal, deletion) and the accounts under «Staff» (add, change role, revoke access) — except a Superadministrator's role and row.

The Superadministrator: everything the Administrator does, plus the technical settings that can stop the service — «How often the site checks», «The database's limits», the thresholds in «This month's budget» and «Anti-bot» — and naming another Superadministrator. A task in this guide that needs this role starts with “Role needed: Superadministrator”; if you do not have it, ask a Superadministrator to do it.

tasks.title: What cannot be done
steps: Nobody changes a participant's confirmed email address, not even an Administrator.
Nobody merges two registrations into one.
Nobody on the team signs the declaration for the participant: at the desk you only record the paper declaration they signed themselves.
No legal text takes effect without an approved version; without approved terms, notice and declaration nobody can register.

Nobody goes past the number of places: there is no registration over capacity, not by hand and not at the desk. A place is given only when it is free; when none is, «Send them the offer» and «Give them a place now» add, once you confirm, a single supplementary place, in the open, written in the trail.

Nobody gets a place without their own signature (a parent's, for a minor): a waiting-list offer is accepted and signed by the person, from their email, and at the desk «Give a place» confirms only on the paper declaration they sign there, in person.

sections.title: Race day — the number pickup desk
sections.who: Volunteer, Organizer and every other role. On a phone.

tasks.title: Open the desk
steps: Sign in (see “First steps”). A Volunteer lands on the desk; everyone else presses «Race day» in the top bar.
Under «Event» pick today's race, then press «Search».
At the top you see how many are confirmed, how many are here, how many have no number and how many are unconfirmed. Those are the race's figures.
Take two piles from the organizer: the numbers printed with names, and the spare numbers, with an empty name line, for people who register at the desk. Nobody who registered online gets a spare.

tasks.title: A participant with the QR code
steps: The participant shows you the QR code from the confirmation email.
Press «Scan» and hold the code in the frame (it works on Android). On an iPhone: open the Camera app, point it at the code and tap the link that appears.
The person's row opens: check the name with them.
Press «Mark present». It asks nothing; a message appears at the bottom.
Hand over the race number from the pile — the number is shown large on the row. To see the number drawn: «Show the race number (BIB)».
For the next one: «Back to the desk».

tasks.title: No QR: search by name
steps: In the «Name, number or code» box type part of the name, the race number or the code from the email.
Press «Search».
On the right row: «Mark present», then hand over the number.

tasks.title: They have not signed the declaration
steps: The row says «Așteaptă semnarea declarației» (awaiting the declaration) or «Așteaptă confirmarea emailului» (awaiting the email confirmation).
Give them the printed declaration form. They read it and sign it themselves. A minor: the parent or guardian signs too, each with their own document.
Press «Confirm on paper», then «Confirm on paper» again in the window.

If the person gets the place, they get the confirmation email, with the QR code, the number and the copy of the declaration; the sign-the-declaration email is not sent. If there is no place, they go on the waiting list, get no email now, and the offer comes by email if they are offered a place.
Then «Mark present» and the number. Keep the signed sheet for the organizer.

tasks.title: No race number
steps: In the «Race number (BIB)» box on their row type a free number.
Press «Save no.» and confirm in the window. A number somebody else already has is refused — pick another.

tasks.title: Never registered
steps: Press «Add somebody».
Fill in the first name, the last name, the birth date, the phone and «Participant email address».
The «This person is at the desk…» tick is already set — leave it.
Tick «I confirm this person asked me to register them…».

«Number given now» already holds the next spare number. Take that bib from the spare pile and write their name on its empty line in marker. Handing out another number? Change it in the box. No spares left? Type the number you hand out, or leave the box empty and the site picks one.
Press «Add the registration» and confirm in the window.
Give them the paper declaration to sign, then «Mark present» and hand them the bib.

Event full, or somebody already on the waiting list? The person joins the list, like anyone. «Give a place» works only when a place is free, and confirms them on the paper declaration they sign at the desk.

tasks.title: Pressed the wrong thing
steps: On the same row press «Undo».
Everything you press stays in the registration's history, with your name. Nothing is lost.

tasks.title: A red box: cancelled or expired registration
steps: The person no longer has a place, even with the email in hand: give no number and do not mark them present.
If it says the number was printed, pull that bib from the pile — numbers are never reused.
Call an organizer. If places are left, you register them again with «Add somebody».

tasks.title: What you do not do at the desk (and that is fine)
steps: You see no email addresses, and you do not cancel, erase or export lists. For those, call an Administrator.

sections.title: Copywriter — the events' texts and the pages
sections.who: Role: Copywriter (Redactor). You write; you do not configure or publish.

tasks.title: Correct an event's text
steps: «Events» → «Edit» on the event's row.
Open the card with the text: «Title and summary», «Event description» or «Programme, rules and declaration» (then «The day's programme and what to bring» or «Rules»).
Write in the «Română» tab and in the «English» tab.
At the bottom, on a published event, tick «I understand that I am editing published content.».
Press «Save». It is on the site at once, in both languages.

tasks.title: Put a picture in the text
steps: In the text editor put the cursor where the picture goes.
Press «Picture» in the editor's toolbar.
Under «Quality» leave «Medium (recommended)».
Press «Choose the picture» and pick the file. A picture already uploaded comes from «From gallery».
Write «What the picture shows (alt text)», then «Done».
Press «Save».

tasks.title: Add a YouTube film
steps: In the editor's toolbar press «Add a YouTube film».
Paste the address into «The film's address (YouTube)» and press «Add the film».
Press the film to write its «Caption (under the film)».
Press «Save». On the page the film loads only when the reader presses it.

tasks.title: Write a page of the site
steps: «Pages» → «New page».
Write the title and the text in Romanian and in English, then press «New page».
On its page, after every change, «Save».
When it is ready, «Trimite spre verificare» (submit for review). The Administrator publishes it.

tasks.title: The two-languages rule
steps: An event is not published without a title and a summary in Romanian and in English.

An optional text (the description, the rules, the programme's notes, the SEO fields) is written in both languages or neither: the save refuses one language only and points at the empty box, with everything you typed kept.
If the English text is identical to the Romanian one, the editor asks whether it is translated — a warning only.

The English in one press: write everything in Romanian, then press «Copy and translate everything: RO → EN» at the top of the editor (event, page, album, team card). Every text goes, translated, into its English box, with the same layout. Read, correct, then «Save». If the button is grey, the DeepL key is not set yet or its credit is spent: the line under it says which. If the English already has text, you choose «Replace everything» or «Only the empty ones».

tasks.title: What is not yours
steps: The event's settings (date, place, places, registration), publishing, the gallery and the registrations. If a text depends on a wrong setting, tell the Administrator.

sections.title: Organizer — registrations, numbers, messages
sections.who: Role: Organizer (Organizator). You see the events and every registration, and work with the numbers, the messages and the desk; you do not change the event.

tasks.title: See who registered
steps: Press «Registrations» in the top bar.
Under «Events» pick the event (or «All events»), under «Status» what you need, then «Filter».
Looking for someone: type part of the name in «Search by name» and press «Filter». With no event chosen, it looks in every event.
The «How far» column says each person's step. Press a name to open the registration: «The registration's journey» and «Timeline» say everything that happened.
The «Until when» column says until when each one can sign, accept or confirm — the same time as the registration's timeline.
Someone asks where their registration stands: open it and tell them what «What to tell them» says — the same words they read themselves. «Copy» puts them on the clipboard, for a message.
The top says once what you cannot change here. The Tehnic role does not see registrations at all.

On the event's public page, the first number counts the registrations holding a place: the confirmed plus those still in progress — a declaration not signed yet, a waiting-list offer not accepted yet, a place a family holds. After the dash the line names only what exists: how many are confirmed and how many in progress, and how many free places are kept for the waiting list, for example “6 registered of 10 places — 4 confirmed, 2 completing their registration, 4 places kept for the waiting list”.

Places kept are free places the waiting list claims, and the card shows them in two ways. With more places free than people waiting, the card says «Places are given from the waiting list» and counts no free place. When the list claims every free place, as in the example, the card says the places are taken — “Thank you! All 10 places are taken — … already waiting.” — and offers «Join the waiting list», while the places line still names “4 places kept for the waiting list”. Either way those places are free: with «Places from the waiting list are allocated automatically» on «No» the club hands them out, with «Send them the offer»; on «Yes» the queue does, to the first on the list. With «Show publicly how many are waiting» unticked on the event, neither the card, nor the page, nor the people on the list learn how many wait: the card says “Thank you! All 10 places are taken. Join the waiting list.”, and the places line no longer says how many are on the list.

At an event with a set number of places, the «Who's coming» title counts, like the first number, everyone with a place while registration is open. The table holds only those who ticked that they want to appear on it, mostly the confirmed, so the title and the rows differ. On the card, “1 place offered from the waiting list” is a place sent to somebody on the list who has not accepted it yet.

tasks.title: What to tell someone who asks
steps: Someone asks where their registration stands — on the phone, by message or at the desk: «Registrations» → search the name → open the registration. The Administrator and the Organizer see it alike.
